Covered this a bit in another post but why not. I could probably talk about this stuff for hours.

Workout in the morning if I can, mostly at home (I'm fortunate enough to have space for a power rack, bench, barbell, weights and some other stuff). If I know I'm going to have a hard day at work or need to get up early in the morning I'll do it at night.

Cutting diet is about 2,000-2,500 Calories. During bulking I don't really keep track of calories as strictly, but it's usually somewhere around 3,500-5,000. Whether gaining weight or losing it I try to do it as fast as I can (usually >2 lb per week). I don't think it's optimal, but it's fun for me and keeps it interesting.

Pre-workout is Chicken, Eggs, Bananas, and some vegetables (I'm quite fond of spinach and carrots). Supplements taken are a multivitamin, a bee pollen capsule, and 5mg of creatine monohydrate powder form. Occasionally, instead of chicken&eggs I might have salmon or bison/beef (in the latter's case I take a fish oil capsule too).

Post workout is a protein shake. What I put in it varies depends on whether I'm trying to gain weight or lose it. Right now I'm trying to lose it; so it's two cups of whole milk, two scoops of whey, two bananas, and some raw honey. When trying to gain weight it's four cups of whole milk, two scoops of whey, two bananas, two teaspoons of raw honey, and two tablespoons of peanut butter (a grand total of 1300 calories, and a bit of a bitch to get all down some days). Take a fish oil capsule too.

When bulking, I'll eat some other stuff once I stop feeling queasy from the giant beetus-level protein shake. I don't really care what because at this point I'm forcing myself to eat anyway, so it's very unlikely I'm going to overeat at this point. If it has calories and I think it'll help me recover, I'll eat it.

When on a cut, for the rest of the day it's usually just fiber-rich vegetables. I have a big bag of frozen peas in my freezer right now. I like to put some in a plastic bag with some ice and eat them for lunch. If I have any secret to my diet that allows me to halve my calories and still manage to train in the morning and then work a physical job right after, it's fiber-rich vegetables. Without them I can't stay focused and feel out of energy.

Oh and on the subject of fiber, if anyone reading this happens to be overweight or trying to lose weight for whatever reason and someone suggests to them that you eat bread (ANY kind of bread, whole wheat, white, gluten-free meme variety, whatever), please punch them in the fucking face for me. Grains are the dumbest source of fiber in existence. A lot of calorie-dense vegetables out there have been getting flak in recent years, especially by the whole paleo thing that's anti-legume. It's a vegetable. How many people can honestly say eating more vegetables is bad for their diet?

Occasionally I drink some coffee if I'm feeling particularly tired that day. But overall I usually avoid caffeine. It doesn't go well with creatine in the long run, and drinking enough water for both is going to make working without going to the restroom every hour rather difficult.

I have considered taking TRT (if you're unaware of what that is, basically steroids), but I'm still on the fence about it. The gym owner at a place I go to from time to time was a former multi-ply competitor at Westside Barbell and swears up and down that there are no long term side effects worth worrying about. But we hear a lot about how women taking birth control pills can't naturally produce estrogen anymore, so I can't imagine that taking testosterone can be that much better. Besides, I have a history of addictive behavior with alcohol and my state leads the nation in opioid deaths, so needles with stuff in them kind of put me off. Right now my numbers are still too low anyway, and at the very least I'd like to get a decent total naturally before I did, if I did.

Programming-wise I usually just do my own stuff. I did Starting Strength for most of my novice gains, have done Texas Method and 5/3/1 a bit too. But I find it's more fun to decide for myself what I want to do that day, and usually focus on one of the big four for four days of the week+a light bench/recovery day at the end to give myself more space between deadlift day and squat day, and to keep myself benching twice a week to maintain technique. I have a bunch of word docs on my computer I've created in the past few years detailing each of the mesocyles/microcycles/splits I've planned out, and usually I end up changing it a bit every few months. If anyone's interested I could go a bit more in depth as to what the actual workouts entail, but that's a bit off-topic.
